reviewStatus: Drafted from verified sources; pending independent clinician review before clinical release.
commonErrors: Grading walking limited by non-myelopathic causes.
Ignoring the employment criteria in grades 2–3.
name: Nurick Grade

version.label: Nurick grade (1972)
version.detail: Six grades (0–5) based mainly on walking ability and employment.

purpose: Grades disability from cervical spondylotic myelopathy.
intendedPopulation: Adults with cervical spondylosis and suspected or confirmed myelopathy.

options.label: Root signs or symptoms; no evidence of cord involvement
Signs of cord involvement; no difficulty walking
Slight difficulty walking; does not prevent full-time employment
Difficulty walking prevents full-time employment or all housework; walks without help
Walks only with someone's help or a frame

resultStates.label: Grade 2
resultStates.summary: Slight walking difficulty; full-time work possible.

resultStates.label: Grade 3
resultStates.summary: Walking difficulty limits work or housework; walks unaided.

resultStates.label: Grade 4
resultStates.summary: Walks only with help or a frame.

clinicalContext.text: A simple disability grade for cervical myelopathy, centred on gait.

clinicalInsights.text: Hand function is not assessed; the mJOA captures upper limb function (under review in this app).

limitations.text: Gait-focused: upper limb and bladder function are not graded.

limitations: Coarse steps are insensitive to small changes.

guideSections.what: A six-grade scale of disability from cervical myelopathy, based on walking.
guideSections.howToPerform: Select the grade that best describes walking and work limitation.

sources.citation: Nurick S. The pathogenesis of the spinal cord disorder associated with cervical spondylosis. Brain. 1972;95(1):87-100.
